searchText: Does anyone know of 89 byte long UDP message spam, alike to discovery, possibly related to dothereum? My home address is getting spammed on port 9000 with large amounts of these UDP messages. TCP dump shows dothereum domains for some of them. <@!194432762315407360> <@!498009160982724610> <@!510413979080720385> fyi; conversation is happening in the nimbus discord, libp2p channel. The dothereum is an older domain in use by Afri, and Discv5 is spamming. Getting messages from 648 nodes, about 1 per 2-3 minutes from each of the nodes. Or it's Kad. Unsure Can you get a hex dump some of these messages? Here's the full log With hex data included It was making Nimbus crash when I ran it on that port 9000 But running on a different port works, and walling off 9000 for now until the spam is over <@!194432762315407360> Can it be that it's spamming so much, since I've been running so many different clients, each with new network identity key material, on the same address? Thus increasing my load? And if so (assumption here), would it make sense to send only so many messages to each address destination at a time? Your theory sounds interesting The client should not crash though If people have implemented discv5 right, there shouldn't be a way you can draw so much traffic because your node identities from the past would just be kicked out of other nodes' tables soon after they disappear. The packets in the log do not look like discv5 to me because they all have random values at byte index 32. The current discv5 protocol has an RLP size there.
